players.product: AI GPU cloud (liquid + air-cooled data centers; 5 GW secured power, target 150k GPUs)

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal Q4 (June quarter) revenue was $137.2 million including AI cloud revenue of $70.5 million. Total revenue fell $7.6 million sequentially as mining hardware was decommissioned ahead of GPU installations, partially offset by AI cloud growth; cost of revenue fell $6.6 million on lower electricity use from reduced mining. Net loss was $684 million, driven largely by non-cash impairments of $450.4 million mostly from decommissioning mining hardware plus a $102.1 million decrease in the fair value of mining hardware held for sale - both costs of transitioning existing sites to AI cloud. Mining operations are expected to be effectively decommissioned by the end of December 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 revenue $137.2M (AI cloud $70.5M); net loss $684M incl. $450.4M non-cash impairments and $102.1M fair-value decrease on mining hardware

quarterly_data.signal: Contracted ARR is the headline: IREN exited Q4 at roughly $0.5 billion of ARR, is at $1 BILLION TODAY following Microsoft's acceptance of Horizon 1, and expects MORE THAN $4 BILLION OF ARR by the end of the December quarter - all of it already under contract and including delivery of Horizons 2 through 4. That $4 billion excludes revenue expected to ramp in 2027, such as the $700 MILLION OF ARR associated with the NVIDIA cloud contract. A significant amount of December capacity arrives late in the quarter, so the reported revenue effect comes through predominantly in the March quarter. Management emphasised that the $4 billion comes from LESS THAN 10% of its 5-gigawatt-plus portfolio of grid-secured connections, and that 2026 capacity is largely sold out.
quarterly_data.figure: $1B ARR operating today; >$4B ARR contracted by end of December quarter; excludes $700M ARR from the NVIDIA cloud contract ramping in 2027

quarterly_data.signal: FY2027 capital expenditure is guided to approximately $25 BILLION TO $30 BILLION for the financial year to June 2027. That covers all capex for the 2026 deployments behind the $4 billion ARR target, data center and GPU capex for the remaining air-cooled deployments across calendar 2027, and a significant portion of the capex for liquid-cooled deployments in the second half of calendar 2027 - but NOT the GPU compute for those new liquid-cooled facilities, which falls into the following year's plan. Within that estimate, data center and GPU capex requirements are expected to be up approximately 15% TO 20% for ongoing and new deployments, with revenue increases expected to ultimately outpace those cost increases. Fiscal Q1 cash SG&A is expected to rise approximately $40-50 million sequentially as IREN invests ahead of revenue across sales and marketing, R&D, development, site and cloud operations.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2027 capex guidance $25B-$30B; data center and GPU capex requirements up ~15-20%; Q1 cash SG&A up ~$40M-$50M sequentially

quarterly_data.signal: Compute pricing has re-rated sharply. THREE-YEAR CONTRACT PRICING IS UP ABOUT 125% SINCE NOVEMBER and five-year pricing up about 70%. Recent three-year contracts are pricing IN EXCESS OF $20 MILLION PER MEGAWATT of IT load - paying back the compute investment in around two years - while active discussions are now at AROUND $25 MILLION PER MEGAWATT, described as consistent across live customer conversations with continued upward pressure and very strong competitive tension for near-term megawatts. Recent customer prepayments are funding 45% TO 55% of GPU capex. Management stressed these are three-to-five-year deals, not two-year or spot capacity, and that it is deliberately NOT sitting on capacity to time a spot price; shorter-duration and on-demand sit above this as further upside in due course. Pricing is described as consistent globally, with possible additional scarcity in Spain and Australia from sovereign AI demand. CEO Daniel Roberts noted the announced pricing relates to GPUs ordered some time ago, so it reflects genuine price increases rather than pass-through of GPU cost inflation.
quarterly_data.figure: 3-year contract pricing +~125% since November, 5-year +~70%; recent 3-year deals >$20M per MW of IT load, active discussions ~$25M per MW; prepayments funding 45-55% of GPU capex

quarterly_data.signal: Build-out targets: roughly 300 MEGAWATTS of IT load delivered in 2026 and another 0.5 GIGAWATT in 2027, taking the platform to around 1.2-1.25 gigawatts of gross capacity in 2027, with more than 4,000 people mobilised across active sites in Texas, British Columbia, Oklahoma, South Australia and Spain. HORIZON 1 WAS DELIVERED TO MICROSOFT - the first of four 50-megawatt liquid-cooled deployments at Childress - and achieved NVIDIA EXEMPLAR CLOUD STATUS ON GB300 NVL72. Horizon 2 is working toward commissioning and Horizons 3 and 4 are in late construction, all three targeting delivery in the December quarter. At Childress, retrofit and GPU installs run in parallel on air-cooled halls; at Mackenzie GPUs are racked across the first two buildings; at Prince George the air-cooled fleet is fully commissioned with liquid-cooled installation underway. For 2027: Sweetwater 1 is in full swing with the first building going up and the primary substation progressing, Horizons 5 and 6 civils are underway, another 250 megawatts of air-cooled conversion is progressing, and IREN has DECIDED TO CONVERT ALL OF CANAL FLATS TO LIQUID COOLING FOR GB300s. For 2028, Sweetwater 2 and Kiowa in the U.S., Bundey in South Australia and Badajoz in Spain represent roughly 300 megawatts, Badajoz being the flagship of the Nostrum portfolio closed during the quarter. More than 5 gigawatts is announced with a multi-gigawatt development pipeline behind it.
quarterly_data.figure: ~300MW IT load delivered in 2026 and ~0.5GW in 2027 (~1.2-1.25GW gross in 2027); Horizon 1 delivered to Microsoft; >5GW announced

quarterly_data.signal: GPU financing is now proven at both ends of the credit spectrum: $6.5 BILLION raised in the past three months, which with prepayments is more than 100% of the associated GPU capex. For the Microsoft contract IREN raised $3.6 BILLION of INVESTMENT-GRADE GPU financing at a weighted average of about 6%, funding roughly 96% of the associated GPU capex with prepayments. For non-investment-grade deployments it closed $2.8 BILLION of equipment financing including $2.4 billion at a 9% FIXED RATE for Mackenzie, led by BLUE OWL and funds managed by PIMCO, with a delayed-draw term loan alongside senior secured notes funding 90% of that GPU capex - and $2.8 billion of it needed no investment-grade offtake yet still priced in the single digits. Over the past 12 months IREN secured circa $19 billion of funding: nearly $16 billion across customer prepayments, GPU financing and convertible notes plus approximately $3 billion of equity. Cash at 30 June was $7.6 billion, of which $1.7 billion is restricted and mostly set aside for Microsoft GPU capex; roughly $14 billion of cash plus committed GPU financing and prepayments is in hand, with a further ~$8 billion of GPU financing and prepayments targeted. Notably, 100% OF IREN'S DATA CENTER PORTFOLIO REMAINS UNENCUMBERED, including Horizons 1 through 4, as a future financing asset base.
quarterly_data.figure: $6.5B of GPU financing in three months; $3.6B investment-grade at ~6%; $2.8B non-IG incl. $2.4B at 9% fixed (Blue Owl/PIMCO); ~$19B funding secured over 12 months; $7.6B cash at 30 June

quarterly_data.signal: Customer base broadened materially. New multiyear cloud contracts were signed with COHERE, PROMETHEUS, PERPLEXITY, FIGURE AI, FAL AI and HIGGSFIELD AI, plus a LEADING FRONTIER AI LAB whose name cannot yet be disclosed - a new contract separate from Prometheus, who IREN can now name as the previously unnamed AI developer from its July announcement. Existing customers TOGETHER AI and FIREWORKS AI have both RENEWED AND EXPANDED. Management framed the strategy as starting concentrated with large customers for fastest scale and deliberately broadening into hyperscalers, enterprises, AI developers and now frontier labs across both training and inference, with the goal of a deep diversified base all holding master service agreements. Prometheus and Figure are highlighted as building for the physical world - robotics and real-world automation - contracting IREN compute to do it. Management said 'signing deals is not the bottleneck in this market; bringing GPUs online is,' and that it is in late-stage discussions over a significant portion of 2027 capacity with 2028 conversations well underway. IREN has intentionally avoided granting customers expansion options, seeing more value in the optionality than counterparties will pay for.

Data center design and power efficiency: Sweetwater 1 is becoming the reference design for Sweetwater 2, Kiowa, Bundey and later projects, with common layouts and equipment plus more modularisation and prefab, explicitly built for successive GPU generations and evolving cooling INCLUDING 800-VOLT DC, all developed in collaboration with NVIDIA - a direct answer to the bear case that AI data centers get rebuilt in ten years. IREN also expects to extract more from sites it already owns: existing sites have SPARE POWER BEYOND CURRENT DEPLOYMENT PLANS that can support more GPUs and revenue WITHOUT NEW GRID CAPACITY, the scarcest input in the industry, starting with new liquid-cooled installs at Mackenzie, Canal Flats and Prince George in 2027. Tools such as NVIDIA MaxLPS, which smooths GPU power draw, and the NVIDIA DSX reference architecture, which runs chips at higher temperatures without giving up performance, let IREN direct more of each megawatt to IT load. Headline PUE has been deliberately conservative at 200 megawatts of IT load for 300 megawatts of gross capacity, and IREN uses a highly efficient CLOSED-LOOP liquid cooling system with minimal ongoing water usage.
quarterly_data.figure: 200MW IT load per 300MW gross capacity headline ratio; spare power at existing sites supports more GPUs with no new grid capacity

quarterly_data.signal: Software layer: MIRANTIS was named an INAUGURAL NVIDIA-CERTIFIED HYPERVISOR on the day of the call, which co-CEO Daniel Roberts said makes IREN 'the only neocloud certified hypervisor from NVIDIA,' giving NVIDIA validation at the software layer as well as the hardware layer. Commercially, Mirantis opens new customer classes: very large hyperscaler and frontier-lab customers take compute bare metal, but smaller AI developers, labs and enterprises value an orchestration layer on top, and Mirantis also enables ON-DEMAND compute alongside reserved managed clusters plus enterprise support, monitoring and deployment capability. IREN's rationale for owning all three layers - data centers, compute and software - is that each layer makes the one underneath worth more. Headcount nearly TRIPLED in FY2026 including hundreds of colleagues joining through Mirantis and Nostrum, with similar growth expected in FY2027 and five C-suite appointments hired from NVIDIA, AWS, Oracle, Google and other leading data center operators.

On Texas regulation, management addressed Governor Abbott's directive - which targets transparency, grid reliability, water usage and impact on local communities - by noting IREN funded all required grid upgrades at Childress, sited it a number of miles outside the main town with no residential neighbours, and uses a highly efficient closed-loop water-cooling system with very minimal ongoing water usage. IREN said it welcomes the additional transparency and is positioned well with two very large already-energised Texas sites, and expects a tighter interconnection process to favour real and well-capitalised projects. Co-CEO Daniel Roberts framed the macro backdrop with the observation that across eight models tracked by OpenRouter, weekly token usage across large language models increased NEARLY 17x IN 8 MONTHS, which is very difficult to serve with infrastructure on three-year lead times.
quarterly_data.figure: Weekly LLM token usage across eight OpenRouter-tracked models up nearly 17x in 8 months

contracts.signal: HORIZON 1 WAS DELIVERED TO AND ACCEPTED BY MICROSOFT during the month of the call - the first of four 50-megawatt liquid-cooled deployments at Childress - taking IREN's operating ARR to $1 billion. contracts.signal: IREN's Horizon 1 achieved NVIDIA EXEMPLAR CLOUD STATUS ON GB300 NVL72, and its Mirantis software business was named an INAUGURAL NVIDIA-CERTIFIED HYPERVISOR, which IREN says makes it the only neocloud with a certified hypervisor from NVIDIA - validation at both the hardware and software layers.
